result.distinct_grid_states:
TWO distinct equity-index grid states exist on this channel inside 2016-01-01 -> 2020-06-30, and they are NOT in capture order.

STATE G1 — "granular / T+1 to 4.45 am". A code-and-contract grid organised COMMODITIES / FINANCIALS (Dividend Index, Foreign Exchange, Equity Index, Interest Rate), 88 contracts. Nikkei 225 futures 7.30 am to 2.25 pm / 2.55 pm to 4.45 am; FTSE China A50 9:00 am to 4:30 pm / 5.00 pm to 4.45 am; MSCI Singapore futures 8.30am to 5.10 pm / 5.40 pm to 4.45 am; MSCI Taiwan futures 8.45 am to 1.45 pm / 2.15 pm to 4.45 am. Capture range: FIRST 20170705000242 (sgxweb_ch mirror), LAST 20170927124017 (sgxweb English). The extracted tables of the two captures diff to zero differences, so it is one state seen twice, spanning 2017-07-05 -> 2017-09-27.

STATE G2 — "legacy / T+1 to 2.00 am (following day)". A flat CONTRACTS grid with a Mutual Offset (CME) column, 33 contracts, older contract names. Nikkei 225 Index Futures 7.45 am - 2.25 pm / 3.15 pm - 2.00 am (following day); FTSE Xinhua China A50 9.00 am - 3.25 pm / 4.10 pm - 2.00 am (following day); MSCI S'pore Index Futures 8.30 am - 5.10 pm / 6.15 pm - 2.00 am (following day); MSCI Taiwan Index Futures 8.45 am - 1.45 pm / 2.35 pm - 2.00 am (following day). Capture range: FIRST = LAST = 20180711020353. One capture only; the URL has no other content-bearing capture at any date (all post-2020 captures return the modern site's unsupported-browser shell).

THE BRACKETING ASKED FOR CANNOT BE DONE FROM THIS CHANNEL, and the reason is evidentiary, not a retrieval gap. G2 (the 2.00 am content) was captured 2018-07-11, a full year AFTER G1 (the 4.45 am content) was captured 2017-07-05. The two pages coexisted live on sgx.com on different content trees: the maintained WebSphere Portal page (wps/portal/sgxweb/...) and an unrefreshed Web Content Manager fragment (wps/wcm/connect/mp_en/...). This is corroborated inside a single day: on 2017-09-27 the derivatives page (12:40:17) shows the Fuel Oil 380cst contract as 4.45 am while the sibling commodities page (13:30:20) shows the same contract as 2.00 am. So a capture timestamp on this channel dates only the OBSERVATION, never the state, and the 02:00 -> 04:45 changeover must be left undated from portal evidence alone.

THE 05:15 T+1 CLOSE APPEARS NOWHERE ON THIS CHANNEL. The portal derivatives page had removed its grid entirely by capture 20181020041054 (replaced by "For information relating to trading hours, please refer to the SGX calendar 2018 or contract specifications of the applicable product."), stayed grid-free through 20181223111840 and 20181231134425 (same digest), and 301'd away at 20190419132051. The 04:45 -> 05:15 move therefore has to come from another channel (calendar PDFs / api2.sgx.com / the 2019 site).

Three of the five families named in the issue are covered by both states. The Singapore family is present as "SGX MSCI Singapore Index Futures/Options" (G1) and "MSCI S'pore Index Futures/Options" (G2) — never under an FTSE name in this window. The Taiwan family is present only as MSCI Taiwan, never FTSE Taiwan. NO NTR / Net Total Return (USD) contract is named on ANY capture in this channel — searched case-sensitively across all retrieved files; the NTR suite must be sourced elsewhere.

One further verbatim caution: G1 prints NO "(following day)" qualifier on any T+1 cell — the 4.45 am is a bare clock time — whereas G2 prints "(following day)" on every T+1 cell except the Nikkei 225 Dividend Futures row ("6.45 pm – 2.00am"). G1 also mixes colon and full-stop separators within one row (FTSE China A50: "9:00 am to 4:30 pm" / "5.00 pm to 4.45 am") and prints "8.30am" closed-up for the two Singapore futures rows. 1. The URL named in the task brief (wps/wcm/connect/mp_en/.../Trading+Hours with the noCache query) has EXACTLY ONE capture in the whole archive window under any query variant. CDX prefix + collapse=digest over 2016-01-01..2020-06-30 returned one row; an all-time, no-collapse prefix query on ".../derivatives_trading_hours_and_calendar/Trading+Hours" returned 7 rows: the 2018-07-11 one plus six 2021-2025 captures of a "?presentationtemplate=design_lib/PT_Printer_Friendly" variant. I fetched 20210925205725 and it contains no grid at all — just the modern site's "Your current browser or operating system version is unsupported" shell (saved as wcm_tradinghours_printerfriendly_20210925205725_OUTOFWINDOW.html). No further content there.

2. The marketplace-portal derivatives hours URL (wps/portal/marketplace/mp-en/trading_on_sgx/derivatives_market/derivatives_trading_hours_and_calendar) has four captures 2015-2018 and EVERY ONE is a 302 with the same digest. I followed the 2016-01-28 redirect: Location is just /wps/portal/sgxweb — the site root, no hours content. This kills the most promising route to a 2016 capture.

3. No capture of the derivatives hours page exists between 2013-08-20 and 2017-07-05, on any URL, under any host form. An all-time no-collapse CDX on the sgxweb derivatives URL returns 2013-08-20, then nothing until 2017-09-27. I fetched the 2013 capture anyway (portal_deriv_20130820090335_OUTOFWINDOW.html): it is out of window AND does not carry the standard grid — at that date the page held a holiday trading schedule ("Closed" / "Holiday trading" cells). It cannot serve as a pre-2016 baseline for the 2.00 am state.

4. A domain-wide CDX sweep (url=sgx.com, matchType=domain, 2016..2020-06, filter on hours in the urlkey) returned an empty array — the domain-scope query appears to bail rather than scan. Saved as cdx_domain_tradinghours.json for the record. I replaced it with a /wps/ prefix sweep using the same filter and collapse=urlkey, which succeeded and IS the definitive in-window inventory: 14 URLs, saved as cdx_wps_hours_2016_2020.json. Every one of those 14 was accounted for — 3 derivatives-hours artifacts (2 of them the identical G1 state), 4 commodities, 3 securities, 1 home-level page with no sessions table, 1 marketplace 302, 2 unrelated 2019 securities-outage notifications (both HTTP 503).

5. The wcm/connect content tree yields nothing further. Enumerating mp_en/site/trading_on_sgx (31 distinct URLs, all time) shows the only derivatives-hours content items are "Trading Hours", "Trading and Clearing Calendar", "World Holidays", "Earlier Market Closing Schedule" and "2008 Trading Schedule" — the last four captured only in 2009 or after 2021. Enumerating sgx_en/home/trading returned 8 URLs, none of them a derivatives hours grid.

6. The sibling commodities hours page (wps/portal/sgxweb/home/trading/commodities/trading_hours_calender) has only 4 content captures ever and carries NO equity-index rows, so it cannot supply any of the five families. I kept it only because its 2017-09-27 capture is the same-day contradiction described above.

7. No artifact on this channel self-dates. All three grid-bearing captures were checked for origin headers (saved as archive_headers.txt): the portal pages send Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate and no Last-Modified; the wcm fragment sends only an ETag ("561385584"). None of the pages prints a revision date, an "effective from" line, or a "last updated" stamp. The only in-page dating hint at all is the 2017-09-27 sidebar's PDF list stopping at "SGX Calendar 2017" — suggestive, not probative, and deliberately not used to infer anything.

8. Wayback flakiness: web.archive.org refused connections intermittently (curl exit 7) on roughly one call in four. Every fetch used a 3-5 attempt backoff loop and all of them eventually succeeded, so no artifact was lost to transport failure.

result.dead_ends:
THE "NO 2019 CALENDAR SURVIVES" CLAIM IS HALF WRONG — and the half that is wrong is the load-bearing one. The repo's belief was tested with CDX over both hosts and the archive negative HOLDS: url=api2.sgx.com/sites/default/files/2019*&matchType=prefix returns [], and the 2019-01 folder prefix returns ~200 rows containing no "2019 DT Calendar.pdf". But the document is STILL LIVE at its original SGX URL and was retrieved today, sha256-identical to the prior sweep's unattributed artifacts/cal2019.pdf. The 2018 (Apr) edition is live too. So the pre-2020 calendars were never archived, and were never gone. FINDINGS.md's "RECONCILE BEFORE USE" flag on the api2 2019-01 calendar is now resolved in favour of the calendar.

Genuine dead ends:

1. Product pages as HTML — worthless. www2.sgx.com/derivatives/products/chinaa50 (2019-01-16), nikkei225futuresoptions?cc=NK (2019-09-22) and sgxsimsci?cc=SGP (2019-09-30) are all archived, all 200, and all empty React shells with no hours in the markup. Saved as prod_*.html purely to document that. The hours live in the content-api payload behind them, and for the two September 2019 pages that payload was NOT archived — which is precisely why the 04:45→05:15 window stays dark.

2. www2.sgx.com/derivatives/trading — the page the 2019 calendar's own footnote cites for "detailed timings" — has NO capture before 2020-08-03. The obvious surface for witnessing the changeover does not exist in the archive for the relevant era.

3. No content-api capture of any kind touching derivatives products between 2019-06-21 and 2020-01-09. The only captures in that window are alerts, menus, a securities equity page and a screener token.

4. Six further 2019-calendar filename shapes probed live on api2 — 2019-02/, 2019-06/, 2019-11/, 2019-12/ "2019 DT Calendar.pdf", "SGX Derivatives Trading Calendar 2019.pdf", "2019 DT Calendar_0.pdf" — all 404. There is exactly one 2019 edition and no mid-year update.

5. Year-end artifacts carry no grid. SGX-DT Trading Schedules for Year End 2019 and Appendix 1 tabulate T Session / T+1 Session as Open/Closed per contract, never as times. The Titan DTDC Factsheet (Dec 2019) mentions "the end of day T+1 session closing at 5.15am" in prose — post-change, so it corroborates State C's existence but adds nothing to the 04:45 era.

6. CDX for the old wcm portal (sgx.com/wps/wcm/connect/mp_en/site/trading_on_sgx*) returned zero rows in this session under two prefix forms. That surface belongs to the portal-hours-page channel; I did not pursue it further.

One query never came back — the exact-URL CDX for the 2019 calendar — but the 2019-01 folder-prefix query did return and answers the identical question, so the negative is established rather than assumed. Zero-byte .txt and "[]" .json files in the channel directory are successful queries that matched nothing, not failed fetches; INDEX.md says so explicitly.

TWO distinct grids across the artifacts this channel actually opened, plus two artifacts that deliberately carry no grid.

GRID A — the 2017 SGX portal grid, "Trading Hours* for SGX Derivatives Market", 88 contract rows. Seen at capture 20170705000242 (sgxweb_ch) and capture 20170927124017 (sgxweb English). A programmatic set-diff of the two 88-row tables returned zero rows unique to either side, so this is ONE state, and the captures bracket it: 2017-07-05 00:02:42 through 2017-09-27 12:40:17. Nikkei 225 Futures 7.30 am to 2.25 pm / 2.55 pm to 4.45 am; FTSE China A50 9:00 am to 4:30 pm / 5.00 pm to 4.45 am; MSCI Singapore Futures 8.30am to 5.10 pm / 5.40 pm to 4.45 am; MSCI Taiwan Futures 8.45 am to 1.45 pm / 2.15 pm to 4.45 am; NTR (USD) suite ABSENT from the artifact entirely. This is the load-bearing find: the T+1 close is already 4.45 am on 2017-07-05, which means the 2.00 am T+1 close on the WCM fragment captured 2018-07-11 was ALREADY SUPERSEDED nearly a year before that capture. Two SGX-published states coexisted on sgx.com through 2018 — the live portal page at 4.45 am and an orphaned WCM fragment at 2.00 am — and the fragment is the stale one.

NO GRID — captures 20181020041054 and 20181223111840 of the same English portal URL. Between 2017-09-27 and 2018-10-20 SGX deleted the table from the page and replaced it with "For information relating to trading hours, please refer to the SGX calendar 2018 or contract specifications of the applicable product." So for the whole of the 2018-2019 stretch SGX's own answer was the calendar PDF — and that PDF is exactly what is now unreachable (see dead ends). The 2018 and 2019 grid states are therefore NOT recoverable through this channel.

GRID B — the 2020 boundary edition, "Trading Hours of SGX Futures and Options Contracts" in SGX Derivatives Trading Calendar 2020, document-dated 2 January 2020, fetched live 2026-09-06. Nikkei 7.30am to 2.25pm / 2.55pm to 5.15am; A50 9.00am to 4.30pm / 5.00pm to 5.15am; SiMSCI 8.30am to 5.20pm / 5.50pm to 5.15am; Taiwan 8.45am to 1.45pm / 2.15pm to 5.15am; every NTR (USD/JPY) row 7.25am to 6.30pm / 7.00pm to 5.15am. Included only to anchor the far end of the window; it matches what the repo already holds.

Deltas from GRID A to GRID B for the five families, stated as observations and NOT dated: Nikkei T unchanged, T+1 close 4.45am -> 5.15am. A50 T unchanged, T+1 close 4.45am -> 5.15am, and the contract name gains its "SGX" prefix. I also found and tried a live-only variant without the _0 suffix (2019-07/Titan DTDC Newsletter - Extension of T+1 Trading Hours.pdf, 221792 bytes): also encrypted. Their filenames alone are suggestive — an "Extension of T+1 Trading Hours" newsletter uploaded 2019-07 and a "Go Live Schedule" uploaded 2019-10, bracketing the 4.45am -> 5.15am move — but I am reporting the filenames and upload folders only, and asserting nothing about their contents.

Operational note: the Wayback Machine served "Internet Archive: Temporarily Offline" HTML intermittently throughout this session; my CDX helper treats that page as a retryable failure rather than an empty result, which matters because it otherwise parses as a non-answer. One query (the CDX probe for UUID 620b6dca) exhausted five retries and returned UNAVAILABLE rather than [] — but that same UUID also fails the live probe and is covered by the domain-wide .*pdf.* sweep, so the conclusion holds.
